classification.habitat: Tropical and subtropical regions; cultivated and wild

identification.description: Small tree with pale grey bark and feathery-looking branchlets bearing numerous small leaves.
identification.whole_plant: Small to medium tree; crown often light and spreading.
identification.stem: Trunk with grey to grey-brown bark; branchlets slender.
identification.leaf: Small, simple, closely set on branchlets, giving a pinnate appearance.
identification.flower: Small, inconspicuous, greenish-yellow; male and female flowers occur on the same plant.
identification.fruit: Nearly spherical, smooth, pale green to yellow-green, with characteristic vertical furrows; sour/astringent taste.
identification.seed: Enclosed in the hard, six-ridged stone.
identification.bark: Grey-brown and exfoliating in older portions.

formulations.name: Triphala
formulations.indication: Traditional use in digestive and rasayana practice

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Composition varies with cultivar, maturity and processing.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Extensively studied as a medicinal fruit; research includes antioxidant and other pharmacological investigations.
modern_information.safety_notes: Clinical use should consider preparation, dose and individual factors.

exam_points: Fruit is the principal medicinal part
student.quick_revision: Āmalakī: fruit; five tastes except salt is classically emphasized; sheeta virya; madhura vipaka.

doctor.quick_reference: Traditional rasayana drug chiefly represented by its fruit.

classification.habitat: Dry and moist tropical regions; commonly cultivated

identification.description: Tree recognized by long hanging racemes of yellow flowers and cylindrical dark pods.
identification.leaf: Paripinnate compound leaves with several pairs of larger leaflets.
identification.flower: Bright yellow, arranged in long pendulous racemes.
identification.fruit: Long cylindrical, dark brown to black, indehiscent pod containing many seeds in separate compartments.
identification.seed: Numerous, hard, embedded in dark pulp.

dosha.vata: generally not aggravating when appropriately used

therapeutics.precautions: Purgative effect varies with preparation and dose.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Investigated pharmacologically; traditional use prominently concerns laxative action of fruit pulp.
modern_information.safety_notes: Excessive laxative use may cause gastrointestinal effects and fluid/electrolyte disturbance.

exam_points: Fruit pulp is important medicinal part
viva_questions: How is the fruit of Aragwadha identified?
student.quick_revision: Āragvadha: fruit pulp; mridu rechana is a key teaching point.

discussion_points: Difference between Aragwadha and other Cassia/Senna drugs

doctor.quick_reference: Traditional mild purgative drug; fruit pulp is the principal part.

identity.name: Arjuna
identity.botanical_name: Terminalia arjuna (Roxb. ex DC.) Wight & Arn.

classification.habitat: Often associated with riverbanks and moist habitats

identification.description: Large tree with characteristic smooth grey bark externally and pinkish/red inner bark when exposed.
identification.stem: Large trunk; bark smooth, grey outside and characteristically coloured internally.
identification.leaf: Simple, oblong to oblong-elliptic, often with glandular features near the petiole region.
identification.fruit: Fibrous, woody, ovoid-oblong with longitudinal ridges/angles.
identification.bark: The principal crude drug; outer bark grey and inner surface reddish-brown.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Modern research has investigated Terminalia arjuna, including cardiovascular applications.
modern_information.safety_notes: Evidence and preparations differ; clinical use should be individualized.

exam_points: Bark is the principal drug part
viva_questions: Which part of Arjuna is chiefly used?
identification_points: Grey outer bark with coloured inner surface
student.quick_revision: Arjuna: bark; kashaya; sheeta; traditionally important as hridya.

discussion_points: Traditional hridya concept and modern cardiovascular research

doctor.quick_reference: Arjuna bark is the principal medicinal part; traditionally used as a hridya drug.

classification.habitat: Subtropical, semi-arid and relatively dry regions

identification.description: An erect, branched, tomentose subshrub with ovate leaves, small greenish-yellow flowers and globose red berries enclosed by an enlarged persistent calyx.
identification.whole_plant: Small erect branched shrub or subshrub.
identification.root: The medicinal part is the dried mature root.
identification.leaf: Simple, generally ovate to oblong leaves.
identification.flower: Small greenish-yellow flowers in axillary clusters.
identification.fruit: Globose red berry enclosed by an enlarged persistent calyx.
